audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL internals (LOG opcodes, ModExp precompile gas repricing, storage operations, arithmetic) and CL logic (BLS aggregation, validator index reuse, Whisk SSLE, eth/66 P2P, light client fork upgrades). Both layers and their interfaces are in scope.

trusted_external_entities.name: BLS Signature Source via P2P Gossip
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Aggregate signatures received via P2P gossip (attestations, sync committee messages)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Aggregate signatures and public keys arrive from P2P network peers. Any validator or peer can submit signatures; they must be cryptographically verified via FastAggregateVerify. The empty-set edge case (G2 point at infinity) is a critical validation boundary.

trusted_external_entities.name: New Validator Depositor via Beacon Chain
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Validator deposit processing (index reuse in EIP-6914)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Depositors trigger index allocation. An attacker could attempt to target specific reused indices. The SAFE_EPOCHS_TO_REUSE_INDEX time-lock (65536 epochs, ~0.8 years) is the primary defense. Derived from EXT-DEPOSITOR in spec_ca22aab3.

trusted_external_entities.name: Historical Index References (External Systems)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: External API queries referencing validator indices
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block explorers, staking dashboards, and indexers reference validator indices by number. After index reuse, identity changes could cause confusion. These systems must handle identity changes. Derived from EXT-HISTORICAL-REFERENCES in spec_ca22aab3.

trusted_external_entities.name: Smart Contract Caller via ModExp Precompile
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any smart contract can call the ModExp precompile with arbitrary input. The gas formula must accurately price computation to prevent DoS. EIP-7883 increases costs 150-9105% to better reflect actual compute. Derived from EXT-EVM-CALLER in spec_ce43b11f.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer via P2P (Whisk SSLE)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Beacon block with Whisk shuffle proof, opening proof, and tracker data
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block proposers submit ZK proofs (Curdleproofs shuffle ~32KB, opening ~1KB) that must be validated. Invalid proofs must cause block rejection. A malicious proposer could try to forge proofs to hijack future slots. Derived from EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER and EXT-ANONYMOUS-PROPOSER in spec_d0b2f2d8.

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Peer via eth/66 Protocol
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: eth/66 P2P request-response messages with request_id correlation
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Remote peers send eth/66 protocol messages with request IDs. Malicious peers could send incorrect request_ids, forge responses, or attempt request flooding. RLP message structure must be validated. Derived from EXT-PEER-NODE in spec_d30530f6.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via Light Client Protocol (Cross-Fork)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P light client data in pre-Capella or current format
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers may send light client data in older fork formats. Local conversion must handle malformed data safely. Empty ExecutionPayloadHeader defaults must not pass as valid execution proofs. Derived from EXT-NETWORK-PEER in spec_d4463816.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: All public keys must pass KeyValidate before aggregation. Empty pubkey sets must only accept G2 point at infinity as valid signature. FastAggregateVerify must be used for non-empty sets. BLS library must conform to IETF draft v4.

Index reuse requires: (1) current_epoch > withdrawable_epoch + SAFE_EPOCHS_TO_REUSE_INDEX (65536), (2) balance == 0. Iteration order must be deterministic (ascending index). Overwriting validator record must clear all equivocation history.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Beacon API validator queries by index
boundary_edges.security_assumption: External systems must be aware that validator index identity can change after reuse. APIs should expose pubkey changes. The 0.8-year time-lock is assumed sufficient for all historical references to become stale.

Gas cost must accurately reflect computation: minimum floor of 500 gas, multiplication complexity based on operand size with minimum 32-byte assumption, iteration count with 16x multiplier for large exponents. Malformed inputs must fail with all gas consumed.

Shuffle proof must validate 124-tracker permutation via Curdleproofs ZK scheme. Opening proof must verify knowledge of secret k. k_commitment must be unique across all validators. First-time registration must verify tracker.r_G != BLS_G1_GENERATOR. All proof failures must cause block rejection.

RLP structure must be validated: [request_id, [payload]] format with valid 64-bit request_id. Response correlation must handle duplicate IDs safely. Pending request tracking must have timeouts to prevent memory exhaustion from request flooding.

Pre-Capella data must be validated before local conversion. Empty ExecutionPayloadHeader and ExecutionBranch defaults used during upgrade must not pass validation as real execution data. Upgrade functions should guard against double-application.
